applies_why: The judge text resolves a chain-against-chain collision between the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain by pointing to whether the challenger's chain names Joseph, a verse-level stating criterion.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter;
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'never verse by verse' — I read it broadly to forbid any verse-level naming requirement; a narrower reading would forbid only item-by-item contrary-verse matching.
why: Because the rule requires weighing such a collision by footing, never verse by verse, the judge's reliance on the chain's failure to name Joseph as the begetter is a forbidden stating-verse requirement.
